instruction.text: In a biscuit tin, for each custard cream there are two bourbons. Which pair of number lines shows the relationship between the number of custard creams and the number of bourbons in the tin?
instruction.sound: In a biscuit tin, for each custard cream there are 2 borbons. Which pair of number lines shows the relationship between the number of custard creams and the number of borbons in the tin?

feedback.wrong: Which option has a number line that is counting up in twos?

instruction.text: There are five custard creams. Drag the oval to the correct part of the number line to see how many bourbons there are.
instruction.sound: There are 5 custard creams. Drag the oval to the correct part of the number line to see how many borbons there are.

instruction.text: How many bourbons are in the tin?
instruction.sound: How many borbons are in the tin?

instruction.text: In a hotel, each guest is offered three meals a day. Which pair of number lines shows the relationship between the number of days a guest stays in the hotel and the number of meals the guest is offered?

feedback.wrong: Which option has a number line that is counting up in threes?

instruction.text: A guest stays for one week. Drag the oval to the correct part of the number line to see how many meals they are offered.
How many meals are they offered?
In rugby union, each try is worth five points. Which pair of number lines shows the relationship between the number of tries scored and the number of points won?

feedback.wrong: Which option has a number line that is counting up in fives?

instruction.text: A team scores nine tries in a game. Drag the oval to the correct part of the number line to see how many points that is worth.
How many points did they score?
In a classroom, there is one computer for every ten pupils. Which pair of number lines shows the relationship between the number of computers in the classroom and the number of pupils?

feedback.wrong: Which option has a number line that is counting up in tens?

instruction.text: There are three computers. Drag the oval to the correct part of the number line to see how many pupils there are.
